I would keep things simple and steady. In Quzhou County, I would rely mainly on the wheat-maize rotation because I know it, the land fits it, and it spreads my work across the year without making me chase too many different crops. At my age, I would not make the plan too complicated or put too much land into crops that need fine management and heavy hand labor. I would keep most of my land in winter wheat followed by summer maize, and I would leave a small piece for peanuts so I have some cash crop income and a little diversification. I would use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps yield and stability, but I would still manage inputs carefully because fertilizer and spraying cost money. For wheat, I would focus on base fertilizer, a topdressing at jointing, 2 to 3 irrigations depending on rainfall, and 2 pesticide sprays mainly for weeds and disease. After wheat harvest, I would move quickly into summer maize, preferably with less tillage so I save labor and moisture, then give maize enough nitrogen, 1 to 2 key irrigations if the rain is short, and a couple of pest-control sprays if pressure shows up. For peanuts, I would only plant a small area because they take more attention, but I would keep them as a balance against putting everything into grain.
